selected_evidence.summary: Collector configuration validates; rsyslog listens on TCP/514 and the firewall permits it persistently.
Node2 has valid, enabled rsyslog configuration using TCP, unlimited retries, and a persistent disk-assisted queue.
The baseline inventory marker emitted on node2 appears in the required file on node1.
Boot ID changed from be303eb3-eeb6-4466-86f1-fd6406dd7dad to 8488d979-9215-4639-9a20-69409a731a29. The listener, firewall, existing data, and fresh post-restart delivery recovered.
Boot ID changed from 96974ac3-f19e-45f7-9672-e880dd505cf8 to b4b3e683-4ff5-4019-863a-dc0dd969920f. Enabled rsyslog recovered, emitted a new inventory marker, and node1 persisted it successfully.

commands.command:
cat > /etc/rsyslog.d/20-inventory-forwarder.conf <<'ANTRIEB_EOF'
if ($programname == 'inventory') then {
  action(
    type="omfwd"
    target="10.100.198.10"
    port="514"
    protocol="tcp"
    action.resumeRetryCount="-1"
    queue.type="LinkedList"
    queue.filename="inventory_fwd"
    queue.saveOnShutdown="on"
  )
}
ANTRIEB_EOF
rsyslogd -N1 && systemctl restart rsyslog && systemctl is-active rsyslog && systemctl is-enabled rsyslog
